rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. The intermediate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Halve the gradient slope while holding composition endpoints and temperature fixed to identify which crowded pairs respond to slope. This also tests whether the added separation can be obtained within the 10-minute time target.

Trim the gradient window while retaining injection 2's slope, aiming to bring the last peak below 10 minutes without sacrificing its improved separation. The higher starting fraction also tests whether the remaining close pair responds to the solvent window.
Keep the trimmed gradient fixed and raise temperature to probe selectivity of the nearly coeluting pair. This should also shorten retention, leaving more room for a shallower gradient if needed.

Make the gradient one step shallower to improve the two marginal pairs while preserving the favorable high-temperature selectivity. The current last peak at 7.20 minutes leaves ample room below the 10-minute penalty threshold.

The longer gradient improved one critical pair but compressed another, so return to the best slope and lower temperature by one step. This tests whether a modest selectivity shift can resolve both marginal pairs while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Test a substantially shallower gradient to move the converging late pair through its apparent crossover and separate it in reversed order. The early critical pairs improved with longer gradients; if this resolves all pairs, the solvent window can then be trimmed to meet the time target.

Raise the starting organic fraction to bring the last peak below 10 minutes while making the gradient slightly shallower. The shallower slope should help preserve separation of the late pair after its crossover, while the first peak still has room to move earlier.

Test a lower starting fraction with a steeper gradient to improve early-group selectivity while keeping the late pair on the pre-crossover side. This explores a faster route to full resolution after the higher starting fraction reduced separation.

Slightly reduce injection 9's gradient slope to improve both early marginal pairs while retaining as much late-pair separation as possible. This intermediate slope tests the narrow trade-off between early resolution and the late-pair crossover without approaching the time penalty.

Reduce the slope slightly from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to lift the marginal early pairs above R = 1.5 while preserving the late pair's small resolution margin. All peaks should remain within the gradient and well below 10 minutes.

Injection 11 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a shorter gradient at the low-temperature extreme to explore whether a different elution order permits a faster fully resolved separation.

Shorten the low-temperature gradient by one step to test whether the critical pair separates on the steeper-slope side of its crossover. Injection 11 remains the maximum-score benchmark while this tests a potentially faster alternative.

Keep the faster low-temperature gradient fixed and raise temperature one step to test whether selectivity improves its two unresolved pairs. Injection 11 remains the maximum-CRF method; this trial seeks full resolution in less time.

Shift the solvent window upward while preserving injection 14's slope to test starting-composition selectivity for its remaining close pair and shorten retention. The maximum-score method from injection 11 remains the benchmark.

Lower temperature to improve selectivity within the crowded middle group, and make the gradient shallower to strengthen the marginal late pair seen at 25 C. This tests a fully resolved alternative near the fast solvent window of injection 15 while retaining injection 11 as the benchmark.

Raise both endpoints by 0.05 while preserving injection 16's slope and temperature to improve starting-composition selectivity for its single unresolved pair. This should also shorten retention; the late pair's narrow resolution margin will be checked carefully.

Raise temperature one step from the faster maximum-score method to shorten retention and improve the marginal late pair. This checks whether the middle group retains full resolution despite its temperature-sensitive selectivity.

Return to 25 C and raise the starting fraction to shorten the fully resolved method from injection 17. The slightly shallower slope should support the marginal late pair, while testing how far the solvent window can be trimmed before the middle group loses resolution.
Shorten the fastest fully resolved method by one gradient-time step to test its speed limit. Injection 19 remains the benchmark if the steeper gradient pushes either marginal pair below R = 1.5.

The steeper gradient lost resolution, so test a higher starting fraction with a shallower slope to recover separation while shortening the elution window. Injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Return to the starting fraction of the fastest fully resolved method and slightly flatten its gradient to build resolution margin in the critical pairs. This seeks a more robust maximum-score alternative after further acceleration reduced separation.

Combine a shallower gradient with a one-step temperature increase, using the slope to protect the middle group while temperature improves late-pair separation and offsets some added retention. Injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a slope of 0.055 organic fraction per minute, between the fully resolved 0.050 slope and the unsuccessful 0.075 slope. Although the programmed gradient is longer, the steeper slope should elute all peaks earlier, testing the speed limit near injection 19.

Use the final injection to test a larger resolution margin by slightly flattening injection 22's gradient at 25 C, with all peaks expected well before 10 minutes. Injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, and the maximum CRF has already been reached.
